newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end down on interest rates, results.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end down on interest rates, results.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended down on Tuesday as sentiment remained cautious following news reports of higher interest rates and poor first half results of some big-capitalised stocks, brokers said.
"Reports that some big banks had begun raising interest rates, due to the central bank's recent tight rupiah policy, have weakened sentiment," one broker said.
The Jakarta composite index fell 4.83 points, or 0.67 percent, to close at 713.88 points. Decliners led advancers by 80 to 34 with 79 issues unchanged.
Trading was slow, with estimated total market turn-over of 397 billion rupiah.
"The weak market sentiment was largely due to the tight money policy and reports of poor first half results of some big firms like Semen Gresik," another broker said.
Semen Gresik fell 275 rupiah to touch a year low of 4,550 rupiah, with some 2.3 million shares traded due to the poor results, brokers said.
Semen Gresik said on Monday it posted a net profit of 87.37 billion rupiah in the first six months of 1997 against 115.65 billion rupiah in the same period of last year.

The broker said property firm Duta Pertiwi, a member of the Sinar Mas group, attracted market attention after talk that some of the firm's new property projects in Jakarta were likely to start having a positive impact on the firm.
"Duta Pertiwi's aggresive campaign for its new property project in south Jakarta has boosted sentiment in the stock," the broker said.
Duta Pertiwi rose 75 rupiah to close at 1,025 rupiah in active trading.
